facts.statement: Ypupiara is an extinct genus of unenlagiine theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Brazil.
facts.quote: Ypupiara (meaning "the one who lives in the water") is an extinct genus of unenlagiine theropod from the Late Cretaceous Serra da Galga Formation of Brazil.

facts.statement: The only known species, Y. lopai, is known from a single specimen that was destroyed in a fire in 2018.
facts.quote: The type and only species, Y. lopai, is known solely from a specimen that was destroyed in a fire in 2018.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen DGM 921-R consists of a right maxilla and dentary associated with a fish jaw, found in the Late Cretaceous Serra da Galga Formation of Brazil.
facts.quote: The holotype, DGM 921-R, a right maxilla and dentary (which was associated with a fish jaw), was discovered in a layer of the Late Cretaceous Serra da Galga Formation of Brazil.

facts.statement: The holotype was destroyed in a fire at the National Museum of Brazil on September 2, 2018, shortly after photographs were taken.
facts.quote: Photographs of the holotype were taken shortly before it was destroyed when the museum it was housed in was heavily damaged in a fire on 2 September 2018.

facts.statement: The species name lopai honors the fossil's discoverer, Alberto Lopa.
facts.quote: The specific name, lopai, honors the holotype's discoverer.

facts.statement: A dromaeosaurid metatarsus found by Alberto Lopa in the 1950s, known as "Lopasaurus," was lost after 1980 and its relationship to Ypupiara remains uncertain.
facts.quote: During the 1950s, a single metatarsus belonging to a dromaeosaurid was discovered by Alberto Lopa. This specimen, known as "Lopasaurus" (meaning "Alberto Lopa's lizard"), was lost sometime after the death of Llewellyn Ivor Price in 1980.

facts.statement: Based on preserved fossil measurements, Ypupiara is estimated to have reached about 2 to 3 meters in length when fully grown.
facts.quote: Basado en la medida del material fósil preservado, Ypupiara se estima haber medido alrededor 2 a 3 metros de longitud plenamente crecido.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Ypupiara likely consumed fish significantly, based on its non-serrated conical teeth similar to other fish-eating animals.
facts.quote: The describers of Ypuparia suggested that unenlagiines such as Ypupiara and its sister taxon Austroraptor likely consumed fish for a considerable part of their diet, based on their non-serrated conical teeth that are similar to those of other piscivorous tetrapods including gavialoid crocodylians, spinosaurid theropods, and anhanguerid pterosaurs.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that Ypupiara preyed on smaller animals, mammals, reptiles, and fish.
facts.quote: Se hipotetiza que Ypupiara depredó animales más pequeños, mamíferos, reptiles y peces.

facts.statement: Ypupiara lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 to 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente ente 70 y 66 millones de años durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica

facts.statement: The time range for Ypupiara is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Ypupiara is classified as the sister taxon to Austroraptor.
facts.quote: Ypupiara was found to be the sister taxon to Austroraptor.

rejected.statement: Alberto Lopa found the holotype in the 1950s, possibly in 1957, but it was not formally recognized until 2021.
rejected.quote: It was found by Alberto Lopa sometime in the 1950s, possibly in 1957, after which Llewellyn Ivor Price listed the fossil as belonging to an indeterminate vertebrate.

rejected.statement: The fossil was stored at the National Museum of Brazil for 80 years before being described in 2021.
rejected.quote: The specimen was then placed in storage at the National Museum of Brazil and was not acknowledged again for another 80 years.

rejected.quote: The generic name, Ypupiara, is derived from a Tupi word meaning "the one who lives in the water," in reference to a local mythological creature and its inferred diet of fish.
